title: [CI] Adding continuous testing for ECS dynamic templates

timeline.body:
Closes #96713 

All three tests cases are covered:
- [x] a test document containing all ECS fields with random values in flattened form
- [x] a test document containing all ECS fields with random values in flattened form and index is set with `subobjects: false`
- [x] a test document containing all ECS fields with random values in nested/object form

In addition, I added verification that all ECS multi-field definitions are covered by the ECS dynamic templates (revealing two that actually were not).

@felixbarny @ruflin see if you agree with [my comment](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97901/files#diff-5de719b6a576263ffb32a9a7a1754078f91b12abf0d4fe7141faeb7a91e6b66dR365-R367) about not failing if we create multi-field mapping even for fields of which ECS definition does not enforce such. 
For example, we define a multi-field mapping for the [`*.name`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/1a254c2f08a54ca4ef4dac6760934f78ebff3b62/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/ecs-dynamic-mappings.json#L115) pattern. If you look into the [ECS definitions](https://github.com/elastic/ecs/blob/main/generated/ecs/ecs_flat.yml), you will find that many `*.name` have multi-field mappings, while many others don't. Trying to be very accurate will result with many more dynamic templates.

@P1llus I assigned you as a reviewer because I think you were waiting for this in order to start migrating some ECS mappings to rely on the builtin dynamic templates.

Looking at his again I see this version of Strings.toString will in fact use that internal byte buffer, so this looks fine as is.

timeline.body: I get why we omit `nested` mappings, but why do we omit `flattened` as well?

reply.body:
Good point! I relied on [testecs](https://github.com/elastic/testecs/blob/e4b0837b03d9a63ba6e71f5eb715065fc9050770/ecs.py#L49) on this one, but we should test our [`flattened` type dynamic template](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/735329e1108a085ef36734872244e925cc196a01/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/ecs-dynamic-mappings.json#L177C10-L188) as well!

I will add it to the test, but the test values will always be nested under the fields, otherwise this can't work with `subobjects: false`, where the field names are evaluated as root level, which means they cannot be matched against a `path_match`.
@P1llus why wasn't it tested originally? Do you see any reason not to test it here?

timeline.body: Either the assertions or the error logs should contain some hints on how to fix the situation. Something like change ecs-dynamic-mappings.json and add a dynamic template to map field {} to type {}.

A nit and somewhat unrelated to this PR: you could make the dynamic template a bit more compact by merging `ecs_path_match_keyword_and_match_only_text` and `ecs_match_keyword_and_match_only_text` because both are doing a `path_match` now, after https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/96712.

> @felixbarny @ruflin see if you agree with [my comment](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97901/files#diff-5de719b6a576263ffb32a9a7a1754078f91b12abf0d4fe7141faeb7a91e6b66dR365-R367) about not failing if we create multi-field mapping even for fields of which ECS definition does not enforce such.
For example, we define a multi-field mapping for the [*.name](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/1a254c2f08a54ca4ef4dac6760934f78ebff3b62/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/ecs-dynamic-mappings.json#L115) pattern. If you look into the [ECS definitions](https://github.com/elastic/ecs/blob/main/generated/ecs/ecs_flat.yml), you will find that many *.name have multi-field mappings, while many others don't. Trying to be very accurate will result with many more dynamic templates.

Seems like erring on the side of always creating a `match_only_text` subfield, even for cases where ECS only defines a `keyword` field for `*.name` fields.

I think that's fine. While on the one hand, this creates a bit more indexing overhead than strictly required, it brings a nice consistency via the naming convention `*.name` so that users know they can always do a full text search on fields ending with `*.name`.

@rjernst noted that the problem with fetching from main means that once an ECS change breaks this test, all PRs will fail until we get the dynamic templates (or the test) fixed. @mark-vieira raised a similar [concern](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/96713#issuecomment-1603760192).
I see why relying on main is problematic, but I am not sure what the alternative is. 

If we fetch the `ecs_flat.yml` file from a version branch, for example, it means that we can only capture ECS mismatches after it was already released, which implies that we will ship at least one version with dynamic templates mismatching the ECS of the same version (could be more if we rely on manually updating the used version branch and we fail to do that frequently enough).

I think that a state where `ecs-dynamic-mappings.json` doesn't fully cover ECS should be viewed as a bug. Relying on main provides a good way to ensure that we always release both in sync.

#96713 originally proposed that these tests will run **periodically** but I got advices to add them as yet another test in the suite. Maybe we need to reconsider periodic testing of this?

Any proposals or feedback on that are very welcome.

reply.body:
Summarizing a discussion I had offline with @dakrone: if this test starts failing (due to ECS changes or any other reason), the most straightforward and immediate way to deal with that is to open an issue and annotate it with `@AwaitsFix`. This is one very efficient way to get a quick trigger on such mismatches.

In addition, I made sure to output a very clear indication of what went wrong and how to fix issues related to schema changes. Some such output examples:
1. new ECS field is not covered:
```
[2023-07-31T10:11:25,594][ERROR][o.e.x.s.EcsDynamicTemplatesIT] [testFlattenedFields] ECS field 'client.as.number' is not covered by the current dynamic templates. Update ecs-dynamic-mappings.json so that this field is mapped to type 'long'.
...
ECS is not fully covered by the current ECS dynamic templates, see details above
```

2. wrong type mapping:
```
[2023-07-31T15:21:14,413][ERROR][o.e.x.s.EcsDynamicTemplatesIT] [testFlattenedFields] ECS field 'client.as.number' should be mapped to type 'long' but is mapped to type 'keyword'. Update ecs-dynamic-mappings.json accordingly.
...
At least one field was mapped with a type that mismatches the ECS definitions, see details above
```

3. correct type, but no multi-fields:
```
[2023-07-31T11:23:50,141][ERROR][o.e.x.s.EcsDynamicTemplatesIT] [testFlattenedFields] ECS field 'vulnerability.description' is expected to have a multi-field mapping with subfield 'text'. Fix ecs-dynamic-mappings.json accordingly.
...
ECS is not fully covered by the current ECS dynamic templates' multi-fields definitions, see details above
```

@rjernst @mark-vieira please provide input. We can also decide that we start with relying on ECS main and change if we see it is an issue.

timeline.body:
> I think that's fine. While on the one hand, this creates a bit more indexing overhead than strictly required, it brings a nice consistency via the naming convention *.name so that users know they can always do a full text search on fields ending with *.name.

I'm not a fan of the ECS multi fields but I agree we should be consistent. Do we have an understand on how much the overhead on storage is? I guess hard to tell? Assuming a user would want to disable this, I assume they could overwrite it in `@custom` and only have the keyword?

> Do we have an understand on how much the overhead on storage is? I guess hard to tell? 

I can't say anything clever about the actual overhead, only that since the default mapping for strings in Elasticsearch is multi-field, then I assume it is at least acceptable. We are only extending ECS a bit here 🙂 

> Assuming a user would want to disable this, I assume they could overwrite it in @custom and only have the keyword?

Exactly! And since we added `logs@custom` [before](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/62bebfd9d6b8dc7f7534ad81c9c7abb0391676be/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/logs-template.json#L8) the ECS dynamic templates, any path or pattern coming from it will take precedence.

NOTE: this is here in order to handle a single field that was [added recently](https://github.com/elastic/ecs/pull/2219/files#diff-d11ef5cbccc15e12cd888cf21575f47d4293a14f81b9fdf03f631e9cd171d391R125), probably by mistake and should be removed after this is fixed.
